newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank acquisition defended by Fed.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank acquisition defended by Fed.

text.p: Community groups fighting NationsBank Corp's $9.8 billion acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc "lack legal standing" to challenge the Federal Reserve's approval of that deal in U.S. appeals court, the Fed said on Thursday.

As expected, the Fed defended its decision in papers filed Thursday afternoon at the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. Two community groups have asked the court to overturn the Fed's Dec 16 approval of the purchase, and to block next Tuesday's closing of the merger while the case is pending.

Warning that a delay of the deal would cost it $36 million a month, NationsBank on Thursday told the court it should require one of the objecting parties to post a bond of at least $100 million if the merger is temporarily blocked.
The court on Monday had ordered written arguements to be submitted on Thursday by all sides in the dispute over whether to temporarily block the deal.
The groups challenged the deal in court after the Fed denied their request to reconsider its Dec 16 approval of the purchase.

The groups challenging the decision are the Inner City Press/Community on the Move of New York City, which represents Latinos and African-American banking consumers, and the New Mexico Alliance, which represents Mexican Americans and Native Americans. The alliance is represented by Northern New Mexico Legal Services.
NationsBank in its filing accused the New York community group of associating itself with the New Mexico group "solely in furtherance of a forum shopping effort."
Boatmen's and its subsidiaries, including Sunwest Banks of New Mexico. operate 600 branch banks. NationsBank is based in Charlotte, N.C.
